title: Sleep Disruptions and Information Processing in Financial Markets
authors: William J. Bazley; Carina Cuculiza; Kevin J Pisciotta
n_adoption_cohorts_note: Spring DST change: a common calendar date each year for all forecasters; treatment switches on and off within the year.
eligible_reason: Not a staggered adoption. The treatment dst flags forecasts issued in a short window after the spring daylight-saving change, which falls on the same date for every forecaster in a given year, and the indicator turns off again (sample restricted to treat63: 29 days before to 33 days after dst_beg). Specifications are reghdfe accuracy on dst or dst x unprof (or x youngqtrsample, x sizeqtr) with release, day-of-week and user FE, plus time-varying forecast controls in alternate columns. The identifying contrast is non-professional vs professional (or less vs more experienced) forecasters around a common date. Data are not shipped (Estimize license; WRDS I/B/E/S).
design_notes: stata_code.do (Figure 1 and Tables 1-7) on estimize_data.dta (Tables 2-3), ibes_data.dta (Tables 4-6) and international I/B/E/S files (Table 7); none included; stata_code.log shows the published estimates.
data_access_note: Estimize data under license (no redistribution); I/B/E/S via WRDS institutional contract.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (abstract from data/frame/mnsc.jsonl).
